title: John Was the Prophet of the Lord
description: John Was the Prophet of the Lord in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 214 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “John the Herald of Christ”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: John was the pro-phet of the Lord To go be-fore his face; The her-ald which the Prince of Peace Sent to pre-pare his ways.

lines: John was the prophet of the Lord
The herald which the Prince of Peace
"Behold the Lamb of God," he cries,
I saw the Spirit o'er his head,
The proud must stoop, and humble souls
He marks the path that leads to peace,

licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
